cases.title: recursions of depth 600 and less fit
cases.note: Part (1) of the catalogue case, the depth bracket E3a recorded.

given.expr: [10, 100, 300, 600].map(k => ((f) => { try { return f(f, k) } catch (e) { return e instanceof RangeError ? "RangeError" : typeof e } })((g, n) => n === 0 ? 0 : 1 + g(g, n - 1)))

cases.title: the recursion of depth 1 000 that overflows on Windmill fits this engine's frames
cases.note: Part (2) of the catalogue case: on the oracle it fails with Maximum call stack size exceeded. Both engines stop at 1 MiB of C stack, and this one's frames are smaller (JE-48's design note).

cases.title: the overflow is a catchable RangeError
cases.note: At the engine level the value is returned; the pipeline runs the catalogue's text, which holds a ;, in statement mode, so its value is null there (JE-13).

given.expr: (() => { const f = n => 1 + f(n + 1); try { return f(0); } catch (e) { return [e.name, e.message]; } })()
(() => { let v = []; for (let i = 0; i < 100000; i++) v = [v]; return JSON.stringify(v).length; })()

cases.title: a recursion after an await gets the full stack again
cases.note: The limit is measured from where each call enters the engine, here the job loop. Depth 1 000 fits only on this engine's frames (D17); on Windmill it overflows wherever it starts.

given.expr: (async () => { await null; const f = n => n === 0 ? 0 : 1 + f(n - 1); return f(1000); })()

cases.title: a deeply nested bound value overflows when the program parses it
cases.note: JE-49's 127-level check before binding is the pipeline's; the engine itself only has the stack limit.

cases.title: source nested too deeply fails to compile with the same RangeError
the stack size is the configured one: depth 1 000 overflows at 64 KiB
